newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada has long history of peacekeeping.
newsitem.headline: Canada has long history of peacekeeping.

text.p: Canada, leading the international humanitarian rescue mission to Central Africa, has a long history of participating in or leading U.N.-authorised military operations.
It has joined 47 international peacekeeping, observer and other U.N. missions, suffering 103 deaths not including Korean War casualties, the Department of National Defence said.
Among its more noteworthy roles:
- 1947-48, UNCTOK, supervision of election in South Korea, Canada's first U.N. mission.
- 1949-79, UNMOGIP, supervision of Kashimir ceasefire.
- 1950-53, fighting under U.N. command in the Korean War. Maximum force 9,000.
- 1954-present, UNTSO, an observer force to report on 1949 armistice between Israel and Arab neighbour.

- 1956-67, UNEF, the United Nations' first full peacekeeping operation marking the end of the 1956 Suez crisis. Pushed by Foreign Minister Lester Pearson, getting him the Nobel Peace Prize, and headed by Canadian general.
- 1960-64, ONUC, clearing mercenaries from Katanga and securing territorial integrity of Congo.
- 1964-present, UNFICYP, maintaining order in Cyprus. Maxiumum Canadian force 1,126.
- 1965-66, UNIPOM, supervision of ceasefire on India-Pakistan border.
- 1973-79, UNEF II, supervision of redeployment of Egyptian and Israeli forces, maximum force 1,145.
- 1973, ICCS, truce supervision in South Vietnam. Not under U.N. auspices.
- 1974-present, UNDOF, supervision of ceasefire and Israeli and Syrian redeployment on Golan Heights.
- 1986-present, MFO, supervision of Israeli-Egyptian peace treaty. Not under U.N. auspices.
- 1988-90, UNGOMAP, confirming Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan.
- 1988-91, UNIIMOG, supervision of Iran-Iraq ceasefire.
- 1989-90, UNTAG, assisting transition to Namibian independence.
- 1990-91, Gulf War, fighting on allied side with 2,500 troops.
- 1991-present, UNIKOM and UNSCOM, monitoring Iraqi demilitarized zone and destruction of major weapons.
- 1991-92, UNAMIC, monitor Cambodian ceasefire.
- 1992-present, UNPROFOR/IFOR, keeping peace in former Yugoslavia. Maximum Canadian force 2,400. IFOR is a NATO-led force implementing 1995 Dayton accord.
- 1992-93, UNITAF, distributing relief supplies in Somalia. Reputation soiled with torture/murder of Somalis.
- 1993-present, UNAMIR, providing security protection of Rwandan refugees, but failing to prevent 1994 massacre of Tutsis. First two commanders were Canadian generals.
- 1994-present, UNMIH II/UNSMIH, helping restore democracy in Haiti. Canada saved the mission in February 1996 by sending 700 troops at its own expense.
- 1996, organises and leads humanitarian rescue mission in Central Africa.
